scenario: AITA for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money? | My (21F) brother (30M) and I live with our parents. He’s in a shitty job trying to get out so he went back to school and that’s why he moved back in 1 1/2 years ago. I’m in third year university and working to put myself through. I’m in business school which I am finding to difficult but not impossible. I should graduate in 2 years. When I got into uni I started saving for a bit of all my paycheques (whatever I could manage; sometimes it was as much as 15% and others as low as 1%) to go on a big vacation post uni gradation. Probably a cruise, Japan or a trip to different countries in Europe I’ve never been to. It has about $2800 in it now. My brother has not been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. My parents already help him financially so he wouldn’t ask them for more help for that. Last week when he was complaining to my parents about it, they mentioned me and my vacation fund and said he could’ve been doing that all these years to be able to afford to go somewhere, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. 3 days ago he came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or Fall. He said since I won’t need it for another 2 years it’s plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about as much as I do yet always seems to be broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (for the record, I do not pay rent either, which is why I have been able to build up the fund, but I do buy most of my own groceries, as well as pay for all my makeup, health supplies, phone and uni fees). He’s very mad I said no. He says it’s jor fair as the youngest child I got to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He says it’s not fair I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went whereas he had to go back. He says I’ve only been able to save so much money because “mom and dad spoiled me.” I disagree. My father, as well as my uni accounting and finance classes taught me to budget. If anything I think my parents spoiled him Because doesn’t know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don’t think it’s fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he will be able to pay me back in time. Even if he couldn’t roger he could... I’m uncomfortable. AITA?

prediction.raw:
This is a complex scenario that involves personal responsibility, fairness, and Islamic principles. Based on your description, I would rate your decision as **1 (right)** for the following reasons:

### **Islamic Perspective:**
1. **Protecting Your Savings (Mal)** – Islam encourages saving and protecting one’s wealth (*mal*) from unnecessary loss or misuse (*Riyadh as-Salihin*, Book of Spending, Hadith 132). Lending money to someone who is unreliable in repayment is a risk that may lead to financial harm, which is discouraged in Islam.

2. **Fairness & Justice (Adl)** – Islam emphasizes fairness (*adl*) in all dealings. While your brother may feel entitled due to past circumstances, you are not obligated to give him your money just because he is older or had different life experiences. You have worked hard to save for your own goals, and he must take responsibility for his own financial planning.

3. **Avoiding Harm (Dharar)** – Islam prohibits causing harm (*dharar*) to oneself or others. If you lend him the money and he fails to repay, it could cause you financial stress, especially since you are still in school and need that money for your future plans.

4. **No Obligation to Support Non-Dependents** – Since you are not his legal guardian or financially responsible for him (your parents already support him), there is no Islamic obligation (*fard*) for you to fund his vacation. However, if he is in genuine financial need (not just a want), then *sadaqah* or *qard al-hasan* (benevolent loan) could be considered—but only if you are confident he will repay.

### **Brother’s Arguments & Your Response:**
- **"He’s been working harder"** – While he may have faced challenges, that does not mean you should sacrifice your own goals for him. Islam teaches that everyone is responsible for their own actions (*akhiya*).
- **"Mom and Dad spoiled me"** – This is an unfair generalization. Your savings are the result of your own discipline, not just parental support. If anything, your brother could learn from your financial responsibility.
- **"He’s the youngest child"** – Age does not determine financial responsibility. Islam values effort and self-sufficiency (*istiqama*).

### **Alternative Islamic Solutions:**
If you feel compassionate toward him, you could:
1. **Advise Him on Budgeting** – Help him create a savings plan for his own trip instead of relying on you.
2. **Offer a Smaller Loan (If Trusted)** – If you believe he is serious about repaying, you could lend a smaller amount with clear terms.
3. **Encourage Him to Work More** – Since he makes as much as you, he should contribute to his own expenses rather than relying on others.

### **Final Verdict:**
You are **not wrong (AITA)** for refusing to lend him your vacation money. In fact, your decision aligns with Islamic principles of financial responsibility, fairness, and self-preservation. However, you could also consider guiding him toward better financial habits rather than outright rejecting his request without offering alternatives.

Would you like further clarification on any Islamic principles related to this situation?
